title: fix(reactive)!: don't call poll_func when @poll() is applied

files.patch:
@@ -33,6 +33,8 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 
   (#2508, #2515)
 
+* `reactive.poll()` and `reactive.file_reader()` no longer call `poll_func` when the decorator is applied; the first value comes from the first poll, in the first reactive flush. Until then, reading the decorated function raises a silent exception. Reading it from inside an output, calc, or effect works as before: the reader waits for the first poll and runs again once it lands. Code that reads it outside the reactive runtime, for example in `reactive.isolate()` while the server function runs, now raises instead of getting the value; move that read into a calc or effect. For `reactive.file_reader()`, a missing file no longer raises when the decorator is applied; the error is raised when the value is read (#2576).
+
 * `near_points(add_dist=True)`, imported from `shiny.plotutils`, now names its distance column `dist_` instead of `dist`. Code reading `df["dist"]` from the result must now read `df["dist_"]` (#2510).
 
 ### Lifecycle changes
@@ -47,6 +49,8 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 
 ### Bug fixes and minor improvements
 
+* `reactive.poll()` now works with an `async` `poll_func` and a custom `equals`; previously every poll failed. (Thanks, @pcbeingused333!) (#2576)
+
 * On Windows, an output's busy indicator now shows while the output renders. Previously, when a synchronous render function blocked the event loop, the message that turns on the indicator reached the browser together with the output's new value, so most outputs never showed it (#1381).
 
 * UI updates and custom messages sent outside an output or effect, such as `ui.update_text()` in a `session.on_flushed()` callback or in an `asyncio` task, or `ui.insert_ui()` from a message handler, are now sent to the client right away instead of waiting for the next input change (#1889, #21).

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_poll_async_poll_func_with_custom_equals():
+    async with OnEndedSessionCallbacks():
+        poll_invocations = 0
+
+        async def poll_func():
+            nonlocal poll_invocations
+            poll_invocations += 1
+            return {"version": 1}
+
+        @poll(poll_func, equals=lambda old, new: old["version"] == new["version"])
+        def value_func():
+            return "data"
+
+        mock_time = MockTime()
+        with mock_time():
+            # An async poll_func can't be awaited when @poll() runs, so nothing has
+            # been polled yet and there is no previous value to compare with.
+            assert poll_invocations == 0
+
+            await flush()
+            assert poll_invocations == 1
+
+            with isolate():
+                assert value_func() == "data"
+
+            await mock_time.advance_time(1.01)
+            assert poll_invocations == 2
+
+            with isolate():
+                assert value_func() == "data"
+
+

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_poll_first_poll_raises():
+    # When the first poll fails, there is no value yet. Readers must see the real
+    # error (not a silent exception), and a later successful poll must recover.
+    async with OnEndedSessionCallbacks():
+        should_raise = True
+
+        def poll_func() -> int:
+            if should_raise:
+                raise ValueError("boom")
+            return 1
+
+        @poll(poll_func)
+        def value_func() -> str:
+            return "data"
+
+        mock_time = MockTime()
+        with mock_time():
+            with isolate():
+                await flush()
+
+                with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="boom"):
+                    value_func()
+
+                should_raise = False
+                await mock_time.advance_time(1.01)
+
+                assert value_func() == "data"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_file_reader_missing_file():
+    # A missing file doesn't raise when @file_reader() is applied; the error is raised
+    # to whoever reads the value after the first poll.
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
+        path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "missing.txt")
+
+        async with OnEndedSessionCallbacks():
+            mock_time = MockTime()
+            with mock_time():
+
+                @file_reader(path)
+                def read_file():
+                    with open(path, "r") as f:
+                        return f.read()
+
+                with isolate():
+                    await flush()
+
+                    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
+                        read_file()
+
+                    with open(path, "w") as f:
+                        f.write("hello\n")
+                    await mock_time.advance_time(1.01)
+
+                    assert read_file() == "hello\n"
+
